title: R' Yehuda ben Misparta
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Sanhedrin 44a](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.44a.3-4): Rabbi Ila'a said in the name of Rabbi Yehudah bar Mispartah that this teaches that Achan transgressed the five books of the Torah — Achan concealed his circumcision. In Yuchasin the reading before him was that R' Elazar said it in his name, and so it is in the Soncino printing. Hyman says it appears that it was written "R-A" and from this it became "R' Elazar." In [Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 53, section 10](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.53.10), it is R' Yudan bar Mispartah. Hyman considers it plausible to say that he is R' Yehudah ben Sifra mentioned in [Pesachim 70b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.70b.10), and reports that R' Ila'a said in his name that the festival offering overrides the Sabbath.

And in [Chagigah, chapter 1, halakhah 6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Chagigah.1.6.2), he spoke in the name of R' Hoshaya, and from this Hyman infers that he was in the second generation of the amoraim of the Land of Israel.

And so he is mentioned in Yalkut on Psalms, end of the remez supplied as תתם (840 by ordinary letter values): "Rabbi Yehudah bar Mispartah said: whoever answers 'Amen' in this world, etc.", but in Tanchuma, Parashat Tzav, section 9, it reads R' Yehudah ben Gadia.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: Sanhedrin gives both the five books and circumcision statements in Rabbi Ila’a’s report. Hyman cites the Soncino and Yuchasin readings for the form Elazar and proposes an abbreviation behind it.

Both Pesachim and the Jerusalem Talmud say that the offering does not override Shabbat in the statements attributed to Yehudah ben or bar Safra. The [printed notice](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._II._1910.pdf#page=147) gives the affirmative, and Hyman tentatively identifies Safra with Mispartah.

The Amen saying occurs at [Yalkut Shimoni 840](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Nach.840.16), the numerical value of Hyman’s תתם. The [Buber Tanchuma parallel](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Tanchuma_Buber%2C_Tzav.9.2) names Yehudah bar Gadya, beside Hyman’s ben Gadia.
